questions.q: What problem do checkpoints solve in SSIS?
options: They let a failed package restart from the point of failure instead of rerunning the entire package from the start
They automatically fix data type conversion errors in a data flow
They speed up package execution by parallelizing all control flow tasks
They replace the need for logging providers entirely
questions.explain: Checkpoints write progress to a file as a package runs, so a rerun after failure can skip already-completed work and resume from where it failed.

questions.q: Which package property is the master switch that must be set to True to actually write a checkpoint file?
options: SaveCheckpoints
CheckpointUsage
FailPackageOnFailure
CheckpointFileName
questions.explain: SaveCheckpoints controls whether the package writes checkpoint information at all; CheckpointFileName just names the file, and CheckpointUsage controls whether it's used on restart.

questions.q: Which CheckpointUsage setting restarts from the checkpoint file only if it exists, otherwise running from the start?
options: IfExists
Always
Never
OnFailure
questions.explain: IfExists is the flexible, commonly used setting; Always requires the file to exist (and fails if it doesn't), and Never ignores the checkpoint file entirely.

questions.q: What is the smallest unit a package can restart at?
options: A task host container — you cannot restart in the middle of a single Data Flow task
A single row inside a data flow buffer
An individual column transformation inside a Data Flow task
A single SQL statement inside an Execute SQL task
questions.explain: SSIS can only restart at the control flow level. If a Data Flow task fails partway through, the entire task reruns from its own beginning on restart.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft warn against using checkpoints and transactions together in the same package?
options: A restarted package could replay a transaction that had already committed successfully the first time, causing unexpected results
SSIS does not allow both features to be enabled in the same project at all
Transactions automatically disable all checkpoint files on save
Checkpoints only work with MSDTC-based distributed transactions
questions.explain: Because checkpoint data doesn't always align cleanly with what a transaction already committed, combining the two can cause a restart to redo work that was already successfully committed.
